nodes.name: Every 5 Minutes
nodes.notes: Shorter interval than the follow-up sweep (15 min) -- CRM sync is closer to real-time integration than a multi-day drip sequence, so pending rows shouldn't sit around as long. Adjust directly in this node if that's wrong for your case.

parameters.query:
select
  l.id as sync_id,
  l.tenant_id,
  l.entity_type,
  l.entity_id,
  l.crm_provider,
  l.retry_count,
  t.slug as tenant_slug,
  ac.crm_webhook_url,
  case l.entity_type
    when 'contact' then jsonb_build_object('name', c.name, 'email', c.email, 'phone', c.phone, 'source', c.source)
    when 'lead' then jsonb_build_object('status', ld.status, 'score', ld.score, 'qualification_answers', ld.qualification_answers)
    when 'appointment' then jsonb_build_object('starts_at', a.starts_at, 'ends_at', a.ends_at, 'status', a.status, 'notes', a.notes)
  end as payload
from crm_sync_log l
join tenants t on t.id = l.tenant_id
join ai_config ac on ac.tenant_id = l.tenant_id
left join contacts c on l.entity_type = 'contact' and c.id = l.entity_id
left join leads ld on l.entity_type = 'lead' and ld.id = l.entity_id
left join appointments a on l.entity_type = 'appointment' and a.id = l.entity_id
where l.status = 'pending'
order by l.created_at asc
limit 25;

nodes.name: Query Pending Syncs
nodes.notes: One query, same lesson as 20's due-runs query: the three LEFT JOINs are each gated by entity_type match, so exactly one of them contributes to the CASE-built payload per row, and everything needed (payload, webhook URL, tenant slug) comes back together -- no chained Postgres node to strip fields or vanish a zero-match row.

nodes.name: Mark Failed (No Config)
nodes.notes: Marked failed immediately, not left pending forever -- a silently-stuck-pending row with no explanation is worse than an honest failed status with a clear last_error the tenant/you can actually act on (go configure crm_webhook_url).

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ tenant_slug: $json.tenant_slug, entity_type: $json.entity_type, entity_id: $json.entity_id, provider: $json.crm_provider, data: $json.payload }) }}

nodes.name: Send To CRM Webhook
nodes.notes: This is the actual 'generic adapter' -- POSTs a normalized {tenant_slug, entity_type, entity_id, provider, data} payload to whatever URL the tenant configured. Works with any receiver that takes JSON: a CRM's native incoming webhook, a Zapier/Make webhook step, or a custom endpoint. continueOnFail:true -- a failed send is handled by the branch below (retry/give up), not treated as a workflow-halting error.

nodes.name: Send Failed?
nodes.notes: continueOnFail nodes put an 'error' field on the output item instead of throwing -- checking for that field's presence is how the failure branch is detected here.

parameters.query:
update crm_sync_log
set status = case when retry_count + 1 >= 5 then 'failed' else 'pending' end,
    retry_count = retry_count + 1,
    last_error = $2,
    updated_at = now()
where id = $1;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ [$('Query Pending Syncs').item.json.sync_id, $json.error?.message || 'send failed, no further detail available'] }}

nodes.name: Mark Retry Or Give Up
nodes.notes: Capped at 5 attempts total (retry_count is 0-indexed going in, so this is the 5th failure that finally sets status='failed' permanently). Left as 'pending' below that cap so the next sweep just picks it up again automatically -- no separate retry-scheduling logic needed, the existing 5-minute cadence IS the retry backoff.

nodes.name: Mark Synced
nodes.notes: crm_record_id (the external system's ID for the synced record) is deliberately left null here -- a truly generic receiver has no fixed response shape to rely on for extracting it. If your receiver does return a stable ID, add a jsonBody-response field mapping here to populate it.
